headline: Accepted June meeting minutes and reviewed department reports on staffing, station renovations, and EMS call data
summary: The commission adopted the agenda and accepted the June meeting minutes without objection. Chief Curtin and staff gave reports covering July run data, station maintenance projects, recruitment and training updates, and a review of EMS and overdose call data. Commissioners discussed the awards banquet venue and plan to follow up on CRT discussion at the next meeting.
decisions: Accepted the June meeting minutes as written.

decision_evidence.quote: Commissioner McLaughlin motioned to accept minutes as written. Commissioner Chapman seconded the motion. With no objections minutes accepted as written.

plain_text:
Burlington Fire Commission Meeting  
Tuesday August 11, 2026 09:00-10:07 
Members Present: Chair Jake Perskinson, Vice Chair Kevin McLaughlin, Monica Chapman, and 
Ashley Bond (via Zoom). Chief Curtin, Deputy Chief Stephen Petit, Battalion Chief of Training 
Adam Savoy, Battalion Chief of EMS Marsha McCombie, Data Analyst Jeff Nicholson, and 
Administrative Assistant Meghan Sweeney.  
Call to Order –  
The meeting called to order August 11, 2026 at 09:00 am. 
 
Motion to Amend/Adopt Agenda-  
Chair Commissioner Perkinson asked for a motion to adopt the agenda as submitted. Motion 
moved by Commissioner McLaughlin and seconded by Commissioner Chapman. Approved by 
acclamation.  
Commissions –  
Brief commission business included acknowledgments of commissioned individual BC Adam 
Savoy.  
Public Comment –  
No comment from member of public.  
Accept Minutes from June Meeting- 
Commissioner McLaughlin motioned to accept minutes as written. Commissioner Chapman 
seconded the motion. With no objections minutes accepted as written. 
Chief’s Oral Report- 
Summary: 
Please reference Agenda Packet for reports that Chief Curtin and BC McCombie provided 
to Commission 
The following is summary from AI: 
 
The Chief's Oral Report highlighted that the department completed 1,097 runs in July with 6,448 
runs by August 1st, a 5.6% decrease from the previous year. Key updates included the 
resignation of Tanner Studlack, creating a vacancy, and the acquisition of the department's first 
boat to enhance water rescue capabilities, with plans to have it operational by the end of the 
month. 
Station Maintenance and Renovation Updates 
BFD provided updates on several station maintenance and renovation projects. The window 
restoration project at Station 1 begins on the 18th and will continue through next spring, with 
estimated costs around $3,000 for front ramp repairs and $15,000-20,000 for a new HVAC 
preventive maintenance contract. Additional work includes kitchen renovation at Station 1 with a
$150,000 budget, replacement of the basement apparatus bay door at Station 2, and ongoing 
efforts to bring the sprinkler system at Station 2 up to code requirements. 
BFD Station Updates and Training 
BFD provided updates on station improvements, including new equipment at Stations 2 and 4, 
and outlined plans for the Station 3 bunk room remodel with two bathrooms. The department 
implemented a new background check process for ride-alongs and is preparing for upcoming 
promotional processes including Battalion Chief, Lieutenant, and Captain positions. BFD 
reported on training initiatives, including roof rope rescue training conducted by FDNY with 9 
local firefighters participating in a train-the-trainer program, and the completion of rope rescue 
bags for all stations. 
BFD Recruitment and Training Updates 
BFD reported that the department completed their SCBA confidence course and annual fitness 
appraisal, with 5 recruits progressing well and expected to complete training by end of 
September. BFD discussed recruitment challenges, explaining that while they get a good pool of 
qualified candidates, the main issue is convincing them to accept positions in Burlington rather 
than pursuing other opportunities. BFD noted that with increased recruitment funding and a 
focus on local hiring, they are successfully attracting higher quality candidates who understand 
the commitment required for the role. 
BFD Program and Operations Updates 
BFD discussed the lateral firefighter program, noting positive impacts including one member 
who is now leading a recruiting academy, though challenges remain including cost of living 
concerns and two-person engine operations. The department submitted a grant application for 11 
new personnel positions to address staffing issues. BFD also updated the team on ongoing 
projects including the monthly report format changes, infection control program improvements 
following OSHA and CDC guidelines, and the implementation of new Life Pack 35 equipment 
and IV pumps on ambulances. 
Monthly Incident Data Review 
BFD presented monthly incident data up to July, highlighting a total of 741 incidents and noting 
the lowest transport rate in July 2026, which aligns with summer trends where patients are more 
likely to stay at their current location. The discussion covered call categories, with injury trauma 
being the top category, followed by patients refusing evaluations or care, including specific cases 
like motor vehicle crashes and falls. BFD also mentioned that the response team's role was 
discussed, though the specific details were not elaborated upon in the transcript. 
Drug Overdose Response Patterns Review 
The team discussed overdose data and response patterns, noting that while opioid overdoses are 
down, drugs have evolved with over 530 different chemical types now appearing in street drugs. 
They reviewed 31 substance-related events in July and plan to analyze call locations and types in 
future reporting. The discussion included clarification on how working diagnoses are categorized 
and the crew's discretion in documenting incidents. 
Burlington Emergency Medical Services Discussion 
The meeting focused on emergency medical services data and response patterns in Burlington. 
BFD expressed concerns about a city resolution regarding call routing signs, arguing the fire 
department wasn't properly consulted and that better integration and communication protocols 
are needed before implementing such changes. The discussion reviewed patient demographics 
data showing psychiatric and behavioral calls are more prevalent than drug-related calls in 
certain age groups, though drug issues still present significant challenges that fluctuate over time.
The team also examined high-utilizer patients who account for a disproportionate share of calls, 
and discussed the UVM Street Medicine program launching August 15th, though it will initially 
only accept hospital referrals rather than direct community calls. 
 
Old/New Business- 
 
* Commissioner Perkinson asked if there was any updated on the awards banquet. Chief Curtin 
is following up with the Burlington High School contact after school starts to see if we will be 
able to host it there.  
* Commissioners would like to follow up with CRT discussion at next meeting. 
 
Adjournment-  
Motion to adjourn made by Commissioner McLaughlin and seconded by Commissioner 
Chapman at 10:07.
